data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_system_type.Description
data.value: Which machine to emulate. Auto works out the system from the media, which is right for everything except a LaserActive disc and some Pico and Copera titles.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_model.Description
data.value: Which revision of the console to emulate. Models from the Mega Drive 2 on have TMSS, which shows the licensed-by-Sega screen at boot and needs the TMSS ROM in the system directory, named tmss.md or bios_MD.bin.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_sms_model.Description
data.value: Which machine to run Master System software on. The Mega Drive models run it the way a Mega Drive with a Power Base Converter does.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_region.Description
data.value: Region to use when the software does not say which it wants, or says it will take more than one.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_force_region.Description
data.value: Use the region above even for software that asks for a different one.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_ram_init.Description
data.value: What work RAM holds at power on. Random exposes software that relies on uninitialized memory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_m68k_divider.Description
data.value: Divider between the master clock and the 68000. Anything below 7 overclocks the CPU, which some software will not survive.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_megawifi.Description
data.value: Emulate the MegaWiFi cartridge hardware, which lets software make its own connections to the internet. Only turn this on for software you trust.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_io_1.Description
data.value: What is plugged into the first controller port.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_io_2.Description
data.value: What is plugged into the second controller port.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_gain.Description
data.value: Gain applied to the mix of every sound chip.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_fm_gain.Description
data.value: Gain applied to the YM2612 / YM3438.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_psg_gain.Description
data.value: Gain applied to the SN76489 PSG.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_rf5c164_gain.Description
data.value: Gain applied to the Sega CD's PCM chip.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_cdda_gain.Description
data.value: Gain applied to CD audio tracks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_fm_dac.Description
data.value: Which DAC behaviour to emulate. The discrete YM2612's zero offset is the source of the ladder effect, the integrated YM3438 in later models does not have it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_lowpass_cutoff.Description
data.value: Cutoff of the low pass filter the console's audio circuit applies. Higher values leave more high end in.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_overscan_top.Description
data.value: Lines cropped off the top of the picture. Auto crops the region's overscan area, which in some games also shaves a frame off the input lag: the picture is finished before the game reads the pad.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_overscan_bottom.Description
data.value: Lines cropped off the bottom of the picture. Auto crops the region's overscan area.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_overscan_left.Description
data.value: Columns cropped off the left of the picture. Auto crops the region's overscan area.

data.name: Emulation.Option.blastem.blastem_overscan_right.Description
data.value: Columns cropped off the right of the picture. Auto crops the region's overscan area.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.clownmdemu.Description
data.value: Emulates Mega Drive / Genesis, Mega-CD / Sega CD.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_disable_psg_noise.Description
data.value: Disable the SN76496's PSG Noise channel.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_tv_standard.Description
data.value: Which television standard to output in.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_input_protocol.Description
data.value: Which method to read control pad inputs. Not all games support non-standard protocols.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_cd_addon.Description
data.value: Allow cartridge-only software to utilise features of the emulated Mega CD add-on, such as CD music. This may break some software.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_tall_interlace_mode_2.Description
data.value: Makes games that use Interlace Mode 2 for split-screen not appear squashed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_widescreen_tiles.Description
data.value: Widens the display. Works well with some games, badly with others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_lowpass_filter.Description
data.value: Lowers the volume of high frequencies to make the audio 'softer', like a real Mega Drive does. Without this, treble will become louder due to differences in volume balancing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.clownmdemu.clownmdemu_ladder_effect.Description
data.value: Enables the so-called 'ladder effect' that is present in early Mega Drives. Without this, some quiet sounds will become inaudible.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.flycast.Description
data.value: Emulates Dreamcast, NAOMI, NAOMI 2, Atomiswave, System SP.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_language.Description
data.value: Changes the language used by the BIOS and by any games that contain multiple languages.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_hle_bios.Description
data.value: Force use of high-level emulation BIOS.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_enable_dsp.Description
data.value: Enable emulation of the Dreamcast's audio DSP (digital signal processor). Improves the accuracy of generated sound, but increases performance requirements.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_allow_service_buttons.Description
data.value: Enables SERVICE button for arcade games, to enter cabinet settings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_force_freeplay
data.value: Set NAOMI Games to Free Play

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_force_freeplay.Description
data.value: Modify to coin settings of the game to free play.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_coin_limit.Description
data.value: Disable coin insertion after defined limit.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_emulate_bba.Description
data.value: Emulate the Ethernet broadband adapter instead of the modem. (Restart Required)

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_upnp.Description
data.value: Use UPnP to automatically configure your Internet router for online games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_dcnet.Description
data.value: Use the DCNet cloud service for Dreamcast Internet access.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_cable_type.Description
data.value: The output signal type. 'TV (Composite)' is the most widely supported.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_alpha_sorting.Description
data.value: Select how the transparent polygons are sorted.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_oit_abuffer_size.Description
data.value: Higher values might be required for higher resolutions to output correctly.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_oit_layers.Description
data.value: Higher values might be required for complex scenes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_emulate_framebuffer.Description
data.value: Enable full framebuffer emulation in VRAM. This is useful for games that directly read or write the framebuffer in VRAM. When enabled, Internal Resolution is forced to 640x480 and performance may be severely impacted.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_enable_rttb.Description
data.value: Copy rendered textures back from the GPU to VRAM. This option is normally enabled for games that require it. When enabled, texture rendering upscaling is disabled and performance may be impacted.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_mipmapping.Description
data.value: When enabled textures will use smaller version of themselves when they appear farther away, it can increase performances and reduce shimmering.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_volume_modifier_enable.Description
data.value: A Dreamcast GPU feature that is typically used by games to draw object shadows. This should normally be enabled - the performance impact is usually minimal to negligible.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_anisotropic_filtering.Description
data.value: Enhance the quality of textures on surfaces that are at oblique viewing angles with respect to the camera. Higher values are more demanding on the GPU. Changes to this setting only apply after restarting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_texture_filtering.Description
data.value: The texture filtering mode to use. This can be used to force a certain texture filtering mode on all textures to get a crisper (or smoother) appearance than Default. Values other than Default may cause various rendering issues. Changes to this setting only apply after restarting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_delay_frame_swapping.Description
data.value: Useful to avoid flashing screens or glitchy videos. Not recommended on slow platforms.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_detect_vsync_swap_interval.Description
data.value: Notify frontend when internal frame rate changes (e.g. from 60 fps to 30 fps). Improves frame pacing in games that run at a locked 30 fps or 20 fps, but should be disabled for games with unlocked (unstable) frame rates (e.g. Ecco the Dolphin, Unreal Tournament). Note: Unavailable when 'Auto Skip Frame' is enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_pvr2_filtering.Description
data.value: Post-process the rendered image to simulate effects specific to the PowerVR2 GPU and analog video signals.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_texupscale.Description
data.value: Enhance hand-drawn 2D pixel art graphics. Should only be used with 2D pixelated games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_texupscale_max_filtered_texture_size.Description
data.value: Select a maximum size value for a texture to be upscaled, if the texture size is higher than the selected value then it will not be upscaled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_native_depth_interpolation.Description
data.value: Helps with texture corruption and depth issues on AMD GPUs. Can also help Intel GPUs in some cases.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_fix_upscale_bleeding_edge.Description
data.value: Helps with texture bleeding case when upscaling. Disabling it can help if pixels are warping when upscaling in 2D games (MVC2, CVS, KOF, etc.)

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_threaded_rendering.Description
data.value: Runs the GPU and CPU on different threads. Highly recommended.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_auto_skip_frame.Description
data.value: Automatically skip frames when the emulator is running slow. Note: This setting only applies when 'Threaded Rendering' is enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_frame_skipping.Description
data.value: Sets the number of frames to skip between each displayed frame.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_widescreen_cheats.Description
data.value: Activates cheats that allow certain games to display in widescreen format.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_widescreen_hack.Description
data.value: Draw geometry outside of the normal 4:3 aspect ratio. May produce graphical glitches in the revealed areas.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_dc_32mb_mod.Description
data.value: Enables 32MB RAM Mod for Dreamcast. May affect compatibility

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_sh4clock.Description
data.value: Change the SH4 main CPU clock from the default 200 MHz. Underclocking may help slow platforms. Overclocking may increase the frame rate for some games. Use with caution.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_custom_textures.Description
data.value: Load custom textures located in the 'system/dc/textures/<game-id>/' folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_preload_custom_textures.Description
data.value: Preload custom textures at game start. May improve performance but increases memory usage.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_dump_textures.Description
data.value: Every time a new texture is used by the game, it will be saved as a .png file in the 'system/dc/texdump/<game-id>/' folder.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_dump_replaced_textures.Description
data.value: Always dump textures that are already replaced by custom textures.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_analog_stick_deadzone.Description
data.value: Select how far you have to push the analog stick before it starts being processed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_trigger_deadzone.Description
data.value: Select how much you have to press the trigger before it starts being processed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_digital_triggers.Description
data.value: When enabled the triggers will act as regular buttons, meaning they will be processed as either fully pressed or not pressed at all, with no in-between.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_network_output.Description
data.value: Broadcast digital outputs and force-feedback state on TCP port 8000. Compatible with the "-output network" MAME option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_show_lightgun_settings.Description
data.value: Enable configuration of light gun crosshair display options. NOTE: Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port1_slot1.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot A1 (port A slot 1).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port1_slot2.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot A2 (port A slot 2).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port2_slot1.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot B1 (port B slot 1).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port2_slot2.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot B2 (port B slot 2).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port3_slot1.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot C1 (port C slot 1).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port3_slot2.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot C2 (port C slot 2).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port4_slot1.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot D1 (port D slot 1).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_device_port4_slot2.Description
data.value: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot D2 (port D slot 2).

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_per_content_vmus.Description
data.value: When disabled, all games share up to 8 VMU save files (A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2/D1/D2) located in RetroArch's system folder. The 'VMU A1' setting creates a unique VMU 'A1' file in RetroArch's save folder for each game that is launched. The 'All VMUs' setting creates up to 8 unique VMU files (A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2/D1/D2) for each game that is launched.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_vmu_sound.Description
data.value: When enabled, VMU beeps are played.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_linked_vmu_storage.Description
data.value: Enable storage of VMU data on the connected DreamPotato emulator. When enabled, the local VMU save file is not used.

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_show_vmu_screen_settings
data.value: Show Visual Memory Unit/System (VMU) Display Settings

data.name: Emulation.Option.flycast.reicast_show_vmu_screen_settings.Description
data.value: Enable configuration of emulated VMU LCD screen visibility, size, position and color. NOTE: Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.gearsystem.Description
data.value: Emulates SG-1000, Mark III, Master System, Game Gear.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_system.Description
data.value: Select the console type to emulate. 'Auto' automatically detects the appropriate system based on the loaded content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_region.Description
data.value: Select which region is emulated. 'Auto' automatically detects the appropriate region based on the loaded content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_mapper.Description
data.value: Select which mapper (memory bank controller) is emulated. 'Auto' automatically detects the appropriate mapper based on the loaded content. Only change this if a game does not work correctly with the default setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_timing.Description
data.value: Select which refresh rate will be used in emulation. 'Auto' selects the best refresh rate based on the loaded content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_bios_sms.Description
data.value: Enable or disable the Master System BIOS. For this to work, the 'bios.sms' file must exist in the frontend's system directory. When enabled it will execute as in original hardware, which may cause invalid ROMs to lock or fail to boot.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_bios_gg.Description
data.value: Enable or disable the Game Gear BIOS. For this to work, the 'bios.gg' file must exist in the frontend's system directory. When enabled it will execute as in original hardware, which may cause invalid ROMs to lock or fail to boot.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_aspect_ratio.Description
data.value: Select which aspect ratio will be presented by the core. '1:1 PAR' selects an aspect ratio that produces square pixels.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_overscan.Description
data.value: Select which overscan (borders) will be used in emulation. 'Top+Bottom' enables overscan for top and bottom only. 'Full' enables overscan for all sides with the specified width.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_hide_left_bar.Description
data.value: Select when to hide the left column in Master System games. Some games use this column for scrolling artifacts. 'Auto' hides it only when a left bar is detected. 'Always' hides it unconditionally.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_no_sprite_limit.Description
data.value: Remove the per-line sprite limit. This reduces flickering but may cause glitches in certain games. It's best to keep this option disabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_glasses.Description
data.value: For games with 3D glasses support, select which eye to display. 'Both Eyes / OFF' is required for games without 3D support or to display both eyes simultaneously.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_ym2413.Description
data.value: Enable or disable the YM2413 (OPLL) FM sound chip. 'Auto' enables the chip based on the loaded content. Some Master System games use this chip for enhanced music.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_psg_volume.Description
data.value: Set the volume of the PSG (SN76489). The value is a percentage from 0 to 200, where 100 is the default volume.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_fm_volume.Description
data.value: Set the volume of the YM2413 (OPLL) FM sound chip. The value is a percentage from 0 to 200, where 100 is the default volume.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_up_down_allowed.Description
data.value: Allow pressing, quickly alternating, or holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement based glitches in certain games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_lightgun_input.Description
data.value: Select which input method will be used for Light Phaser games. 'Light Gun' uses a mouse-controlled light gun input. 'Touchscreen' uses pointer-based touchscreen input.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_lightgun_crosshair.Description
data.value: Enable or disable the crosshair overlay for Light Phaser games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_lightgun_shape.Description
data.value: Select the shape of the crosshair overlay for Light Phaser games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_lightgun_color.Description
data.value: Select the color of the crosshair overlay for Light Phaser games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_lightgun_crosshair_offset_x.Description
data.value: Set the horizontal pixel offset of the crosshair for calibration purposes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_lightgun_crosshair_offset_y.Description
data.value: Set the vertical pixel offset of the crosshair for calibration purposes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_paddle_sensitivity.Description
data.value: Set the sensitivity of the Paddle Control. Higher values result in faster paddle movement.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_sports_pad_sensitivity.Description
data.value: Set the sensitivity of the Sports Pad. Higher values result in faster trackball movement.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_link_enable.Description
data.value: Run two linked Game Gear systems. Loading one ROM runs a separate copy on each screen; use the 2 Player Game Gear Link subsystem to load two different ROMs. Controller ports 1 and 2 control screens 1 and 2. Only native Game Gear mode supports linking; other systems run normally.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_link_placement.Description
data.value: Arrange both screens horizontally or vertically.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_link_switch.Description
data.value: Swap the positions of the two screens. Controller assignments, screen selection and audio selection still refer to the original screen numbers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_link_screen.Description
data.value: Display both screens or only the selected system. Both systems continue running.

data.name: Emulation.Option.gearsystem.gearsystem_link_audio.Description
data.value: Choose the system to hear, or mix both systems at half volume each.

data.name: Emulation.Emulator.genesisplusgx.Description
data.value: Emulates SG-1000, SC-3000, Mark III, Master System, Game Gear, Mega Drive / Genesis, Mega-CD / Sega CD, Pico.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_system_hw.Description
data.value: Runs loaded content with a specific emulated console. 'Auto' will select the most appropriate system for the current game.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_region_detect.Description
data.value: Specify which region the system is from. For consoles other than the Game Gear, 'PAL' is 50 Hz, while 'NTSC' is 60 Hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_vdp_mode.Description
data.value: Overrides the VDP mode to force it to run at either NTSC 60Hz or PAL 50Hz, regardless of system region.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_bios.Description
data.value: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory. Displays console-specific start-up sequence/animation, then runs loaded content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_system_bram.Description
data.value: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single save file between all games from a specific region (Per-BIOS) or to create a separate save file for each game (Per-Game). Note that the Sega CD/Mega-CD has limited internal storage, sufficient only for a handful of titles. To avoid running out of space, the 'Per-Game' setting is recommended.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_cart_bram.Description
data.value: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single backup ram cart for all games (Per-Cart) or to create a separate backup ram cart for each game (Per-Game).

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_cart_size.Description
data.value: Sets the backup ram cart size when running Sega CD/Mega-CD content. Useful when setting the backup ram cart to Per-Game to avoid multiple larger cart sizes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_add_on.Description
data.value: Specify which add-on to use for CD audio playback with supported Mega Drive/Genesis games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_lock_on.Description
data.value: Lock-On Technology is a Mega Drive/Genesis feature that allowed an older game to connect to the pass-through port of a special cartridge for extended or altered gameplay. This option specifies which type of special 'lock-on' cartridge to emulate. A corresponding bios file must be present in RetroArch's system directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_aspect_ratio.Description
data.value: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_overscan.Description
data.value: Enable this to display the overscan regions at the top/bottom and/or left/right of the screen. These would normally be hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_left_border.Description
data.value: Cuts off 8 pixels from either the left side of the screen, or both left and right sides when running Master System games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_gg_extra.Description
data.value: Forces Game Gear titles to run in SMS mode, with an increased resolution of 256x192. May show additional content, but typically displays a border of corrupt/unwanted image data.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_blargg_ntsc_filter.Description
data.value: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_lcd_filter.Description
data.value: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and Genesis Nomad LCD panels.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_render.Description
data.value: Interlaced Mode 2 allows the Mega Drive/Genesis to output a double height (high resolution) 320x448 image by drawing alternate scan lines each frame (this is used by Sonic the Hedgehog 2 and Combat Cars multiplayer modes). 'Double Field' mimics original hardware, producing a sharp image with flickering/interlacing artifacts. 'Single Field' applies a deinterlacing filter, which stabilizes the image but causes mild blurring.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_frameskip.Description
data.value: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilizes the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_frameskip_threshold.Description
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_ym2413.Description
data.value: Enable emulation of the FM Sound Unit used by certain Sega Mark III/Master System games for enhanced audio output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_ym2413_core.Description
data.value: Select method used to emulate the FM Sound Unit of the Sega Mark III/Master System. 'MAME' option is fast, and runs full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' option is cycle accurate, very high quality, and has substantial CPU requirements.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_ym2612.Description
data.value: Select method used to emulate the FM synthesizer (main sound generator) of the Mega Drive/Genesis. 'MAME' options are fast, and run full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' options are cycle accurate, very high quality, and have substantial CPU requirements. The YM2612 chip is used by the original Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. The YM3438 is used in later Mega Drive/Genesis revisions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_sound_output.Description
data.value: Select stereo or mono sound playback.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesisplusgx.genesis_plus_gx_addr_error.Description

Enabling this will simulate this behavior. It should only be disabled when playing ROM hacks, since these are typically developed using less accurate emulators and may rely on invalid RAM access for correct operation.

This is required by a few CD games that crash if CD data is available too soon and also fixes CD audio desync issues in some games. Disabling this can be useful with MSU-MD games as it makes CD audio tracks loops more seamless.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_system_hw.Description

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_region_detect.Description
data.value: Specify which region the system is from. For consoles other than the Game Gear, 'PAL' is 50 Hz, while 'NTSC' is 60 Hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_vdp_mode.Description
data.value: Overrides the VDP mode to force it to run at either NTSC 60Hz or PAL 50Hz, regardless of system region.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_bios.Description
data.value: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory. Displays console-specific start-up sequence/animation, then runs loaded content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_system_bram.Description
data.value: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single save file between all games from a specific region (Per-BIOS) or to create a separate save file for each game (Per-Game). Note that the Sega CD/Mega-CD has limited internal storage, sufficient only for a handful of titles. To avoid running out of space, the 'Per-Game' setting is recommended.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_cart_bram.Description
data.value: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single backup ram cart for all games (Per-Cart) or to create a separate backup ram cart for each game (Per-Game).

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_cart_size.Description
data.value: Sets the backup ram cart size when running Sega CD/Mega-CD content. Useful when setting the backup ram cart to Per-Game to avoid multiple larger cart sizes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_add_on.Description
data.value: Specify which add-on to use for CD audio playback with supported Mega Drive/Genesis games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_lock_on.Description
data.value: Lock-On Technology is a Mega Drive/Genesis feature that allowed an older game to connect to the pass-through port of a special cartridge for extended or altered gameplay. This option specifies which type of special 'lock-on' cartridge to emulate. A corresponding bios file must be present in RetroArch's system directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_aspect_ratio.Description
data.value: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_overscan.Description
data.value: Enable this to display the overscan regions at the top/bottom and/or left/right of the screen. These would normally be hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_h40_extra_columns
data.value: Extra columns to draw in H40 for widescreen

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_h40_extra_columns.Description
data.value: Set the amount of extra colums to draw for widescreen

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_h40_extra_columns_alpha.Description

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_vdp_fix_dma_boundary_bug.Description
data.value: Enable this to fix the VDP DMA boundary bug

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_left_border.Description
data.value: Cuts off 8 pixels from either the left side of the screen, or both left and right sides when running Master System games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_gg_extra.Description
data.value: Forces Game Gear titles to run in SMS mode, with an increased resolution of 256x192. May show additional content, but typically displays a border of corrupt/unwanted image data.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_blargg_ntsc_filter.Description
data.value: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_lcd_filter.Description
data.value: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and Genesis Nomad LCD panels.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_render.Description
data.value: Interlaced Mode 2 allows the Mega Drive/Genesis to output a double height (high resolution) 320x448 image by drawing alternate scan lines each frame (this is used by Sonic the Hedgehog 2 and Combat Cars multiplayer modes). 'Double Field' mimics original hardware, producing a sharp image with flickering/interlacing artifacts. 'Single Field' applies a deinterlacing filter, which stabilizes the image but causes mild blurring.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_frameskip.Description
data.value: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilizes the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_frameskip_threshold.Description
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_ym2413.Description
data.value: Enable emulation of the FM Sound Unit used by certain Sega Mark III/Master System games for enhanced audio output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_ym2413_core.Description
data.value: Select method used to emulate the FM Sound Unit of the Sega Mark III/Master System. 'MAME' option is fast, and runs full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' option is cycle accurate, very high quality, and has substantial CPU requirements.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_ym2612.Description
data.value: Select method used to emulate the FM synthesizer (main sound generator) of the Mega Drive/Genesis. 'MAME' options are fast, and run full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' options are cycle accurate, very high quality, and have substantial CPU requirements. The YM2612 chip is used by the original Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. The YM3438 is used in later Mega Drive/Genesis revisions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_fm_enhance.Description
data.value: Optional, deliberately non-authentic post-processing applied only to the FM (YM2612/YM3438) bus: a stereo widener to spread the hard-panned FM image, a fixed-point reverb send, and a gentle analog-style low-pass with soft saturation. Adds width and depth to the FM voice at the cost of accuracy; PSG, PCM and CD-DA are left untouched. Fully integer/deterministic. 'Off' leaves the original sound bit-identical.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_fm_voice_recovery.Description
data.value: Experimental. When a sound effect commandeers an FM (YM2612) channel mid-song, the displaced musical note is snapshotted onto a hidden shadow voice that keeps sounding and is faded out smoothly with a synthetic decay so the stolen background note finishes instead of being cut dead. 'Conservative' uses fewer shadow voices and a shorter fade; 'Aggressive' recovers more. The trigger is gated by note age and audibility so it fires sparingly. Deterministic; 'Off' is bit-exact.

data.name: Emulation.Option.genesis_plus_gx_wide.genesis_plus_gx_wide_sound_samplerate.Description
data.value: Select the audio output sample rate. The Mega Drive/Genesis has no sample-based audio hardware and no fixed output rate (sound is synthesised in real time), so this is a free choice. Higher rates raise the Nyquist limit, reducing aliasing and high-frequency low-pass 'smearing', and give better time-domain resolution, at the cost of more CPU for resampling. 'Auto' queries the frontend's target rate and selects the supported rate closest to it, which avoids extra frontend resampling.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_saturn.beetle_saturn_cpucache_emumode.Description
data.value: Which SH-2 cache emulation mode to use. 'Auto' takes it from the per-game database: 'Data only' for most titles, 'Full' (instruction cache emulated, slower) for the games known to need it and for all ST-V games. Override only to test; 'Data only' on a game that needs 'Full' can glitch or hang. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_saturn.beetle_saturn_sh2_interleave.Description
data.value: How closely the two SH-2 CPUs are kept in step. 'Exact' alternates them every instruction and reproduces the previous behaviour byte for byte. The 'Fast' modes let the master run a few cycles ahead of the slave before the slave catches up, which avoids alternating the two CPUs' working sets every instruction, and schedule idle DMA controllers by event instead of polling. Each CPU still executes its full instruction count (within 1-2%), so games run at true speed; measured gain about 15% on Daytona USA and Virtua Fighter 2. Larger windows were removed: they starve the slave and only appear faster. Use Exact if a game hangs, desyncs, has audio problems or renders incorrectly in a Fast mode. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_saturn.beetle_saturn_sh2_jit.Description
data.value: Run the master SH-2's ordinary instructions through natively compiled per-instruction handlers, keeping the interpreter's exact timing. Only with CPU cache emulation off ('Data only'), x86/x86-64 only. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_saturn.beetle_saturn_deinterlacer.Description
data.value: How to combine the two fields of an interlaced signal. 'Weave' shows both the current and previous field together on every frame for full vertical resolution, with combing visible on moving content. 'Bob' shows only the current field, halved in height -- no comb, but half the vertical resolution. 'Bob (Offset)' shows only the current field doubled into full surface height with a one-line offset between fields; preserves the libretro output resolution while giving Bob-style smooth motion. 'FastMAD (Motion Adaptive)' does per-pixel motion detection between the current frame and two frames ago, weaving where the picture is still and interpolating where motion was detected; much higher CPU cost than the other modes but eliminates combing on motion while preserving full resolution where the picture is still. 'Progressive' renders both interlaced fields during the same emulated frame, writing field 0 to even rows and field 1 to odd rows for full-height output. 'Off' has the VDP2 renderer fill both rows of every (even,odd) pair every emulated frame with current-frame content; full resolution, no comb on motion, but doubles the per-frame surface write work compared to the other modes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_saturn.beetle_saturn_mesh_transparency.Description
data.value: Replace VDP1's hardware-accurate (x ^ y) & 1 stipple, used by mesh-bit primitives, with a 50% blend against the final composited surface. The stipple looks like a visible checker on a flat panel (it relied on CRT phosphor blur). Improves the look of smoke, shadows, water, and fade effects in many games. CPU port of Kronos's GL-side improved mesh: mesh-bit pixels are routed to a parallel side-buffer instead of the main framebuffer, then VDP2 composites the side-buffer over the final surface in a late blend pass. 16-bit framebuffer only -- 8-bit paletted mode keeps the stipple regardless. Known limitation: a few games (e.g. Grandia) can show mesh residue for a frame or two during scene transitions where the game suppresses the VDP1 sprite layer through a path the side-buffer doesn't observe; toggle the option off if this is bothersome.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_saturn.beetle_saturn_midsync.Description

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_saturn.beetle_saturn_analog_stick_deadzone.Description
data.value: Inner deadzone applied to the '3D Control Pad' device type's analog stick, in addition to any front-end deadzone already configured in RetroArch's input settings. Leave at 0% if you want the front-end deadzone to be authoritative; raise this if you want a stricter centre dead-region than RetroArch alone provides. The two deadzones compound: setting 15% here on top of 15% in RetroArch results in roughly 28% combined dead-region.

Leave at 0% if you want the front-end deadzone to be authoritative; raise this if you want a stricter pull threshold before triggers begin to register. The two deadzones compound.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_resolution.Description
data.value: Render at higher internal resolution for improved image quality. Lower values reduce GPU load. 'Half' (248x192) recommended for low-end systems.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_renderer_3d.Description
data.value: Select Supermodel's 3D engine. New3D is the current renderer. Legacy3D uses the desktop OpenGL compatibility profile and may perform better on older or integrated GPUs. Legacy3D is experimental and may crash the frontend or fail to initialize on unsupported OpenGL drivers. Takes effect after restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_legacy_multi_texture.Description
data.value: Use eight texture maps for Legacy3D decoding instead of decoding to a single texture. Only applies to Legacy3D and takes effect after restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_quad_rendering.Description
data.value: Render Model 3 quadrilaterals as native quads through New3D's geometry-shader path instead of splitting them into triangles. Requires OpenGL 4.5 and takes effect after restarting content. Ignored by Legacy3D.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_crt_colors.Description
data.value: Apply Supermodel's native pre-output colour and gamma adaptation. This is distinct from a frontend CRT shader, and applies to New3D after restarting content. Ignored by Legacy3D.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_supersampling.Description
data.value: Render each output pixel from multiple internal samples using Supermodel's native supersampling pass. The scale applies on top of Internal Resolution: 2x uses 4 samples per pixel, 3x uses 9, and 8x uses 64. Higher values can require substantial GPU time and memory. Takes effect after restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_timing_overlay.Description
data.value: Show the per-frame timing overlay (PPC/Render/GPU/Total) and log timing averages. Costs an extra draw pass every frame, so leave it off unless you are profiling.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_upscale_mode.Description
data.value: Select the native Supermodel filter used to upscale internal 2D tile layers before they are composited with 3D. At native resolution Supermodel always uses Nearest. Takes effect after restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_wide_screen.Description
data.value: Expand full-screen 3D viewports horizontally to render a true 16:9 field of view. 'Widescreen + Wide Background' also stretches the lower 2D background layer to fill the sides; HUD and upper overlays remain at their original aspect ratio. Takes effect after restarting content. May expose geometry or background artifacts in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_no_white_flash.Description
data.value: Suppress the white flash normally shown when a game disables 3D rendering. Equivalent to standalone Supermodel's NoWhiteFlash setting. Requires restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_av_timing.Description
data.value: Select the video cadence and matching 44.1 kHz audio packetization. Native Model 3 timing reports 57.524160 FPS and uses a fractional 766/767-sample audio cadence; a display capable of matching this refresh rate provides the smoothest result. Native timing requires a multi-threaded emulation mode for continuous audio. Requires restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_crosshairs.Description
data.value: Select which native Supermodel vector crosshair is displayed in light gun games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_gun_input.Description
data.value: Input source for analog-gun games. Standard accepts RetroArch Lightgun, Mouse, and the left Analog Stick through one virtual cursor. Mouse + Analog Stick excludes Lightgun coordinates while retaining both relative cursor sources. Dedicated modes restrict input to the selected source. Changes take effect immediately.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_star_wars_input.Description
data.value: Input source for the arcade analog joystick used by Star Wars Trilogy Arcade. Standard accepts RetroArch Lightgun, Mouse, and the left Analog Stick through one virtual control. Mouse + Analog Stick excludes Lightgun coordinates. Changes take effect immediately.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_star_wars_upright_x_inversion
data.value: Star Wars Trilogy Upright Mode X-Axis Inversion Fix

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_star_wars_upright_x_inversion.Description
data.value: Invert the horizontal analog input when Star Wars Trilogy Arcade's NVRAM cabinet type is Upright, matching the cabinet-specific axis orientation. Disable this when the frontend or input device already applies the required inversion. Changes take effect immediately.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_force_feedback.Description
data.value: Enable force feedback for racing games (requires compatible hardware).

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_four_speed_shifter.Description
data.value: Applied only to recognized 4-Speed driving games. Standard assigns each of the four remappable directional inputs directly to one gear. H-Gate interprets them as Up, Down, Left, and Right, selecting gears from the four diagonal positions. Neutral remains on West and L/R remain sequential shift controls. Changes take effect immediately.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_steering_response.Description
data.value: Applied only to games recognized as Driving. Select the steering response curve; Progressive and FBNeo Logarithmic reduce sensitivity around the center while retaining the available output range.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_steering_output_range.Description
data.value: Applied only to games recognized as Driving. Scale steering around its center. Values below 100% reduce the emulated wheel range; values above 100% reach full lock with less physical stick travel.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_accelerator_output_range.Description
data.value: Applied only to games recognized as Driving. Scale the accelerator from its zero rest position. Values below 100% reduce the maximum emulated pedal output; values above 100% reach full output with less physical trigger travel.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_brake_output_range.Description
data.value: Applied only to games recognized as Driving. Scale the brake from its zero rest position. Values below 100% reduce the maximum emulated pedal output; values above 100% reach full output with less physical trigger travel.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_sound_enable.Description
data.value: Enable or disable sound emulation. Disabling sound can significantly improve performance on slow hardware. Takes effect after restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_music_volume.Description
data.value: Adjust DSB music volume (affects games with separate music board e.g. Sega Rally 2, Virtua Fighter 3).

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_scsp_dsp.Description
data.value: Select the Sega Custom Sound Processor DSP implementation. The modern MAME-derived engine is recommended; use Legacy ElSemi for games with audio compatibility issues such as Fighting Vipers 2. Takes effect after restarting content.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_frameskip.Description
data.value: Skip rendering every N frames to reduce GPU load on slow hardware. 'OFF' disables frame skipping. Higher values improve speed at the cost of visual smoothness.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_ppc_frequency.Description
data.value: Adjust PowerPC CPU frequency to trade cycle accuracy for performance on low-end hardware. 'Auto' follows the game's stepping (66/100/166 MHz): a Stepping 2.x game such as Daytona 2 runs at 166 MHz, which is over twice the CPU work of 70 MHz. Underclocking is the single biggest performance lever on weak hardware, at the cost of cycle accuracy.

data.name: Emulation.Option.supermodel.supermodel_emulation_threading.Description
data.value: Select how Supermodel distributes emulation work across host CPU threads. Multi-threaded runs the sound and drive boards on worker threads; Multi-threaded + GPU also overlaps PowerPC emulation with graphics processing. This is independent of RetroArch's Threaded Video setting. Restart content to apply.

data.name: Emulation.Option.yabasanshiro.yabasanshiro_rbg_use_compute_shader
data.value: RGB use compute shader for RGB

data.name: Emulation.Option.yabause.yabause_force_hle_bios.Description
data.value: Use High Level Emulation BIOS. Not recommended, as it's causing more issues than it solves.

data.name: Emulation.Option.yabause.yabause_addon_cartridge.Description
data.value: Emulate an add-on RAM expansion cartridge. Some games require this to be played, while a few others will have improved performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.yabause.yabause_numthreads.Description
data.value: Depending on your CPU, changing this value can improve performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_region.Description
data.value: Set the Saturn region. 'Auto' detects from the disc.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_sh2_cache.Description
data.value: Improves accuracy for specific games at a small performance cost.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_sh2_clock.Description
data.value: Adjusts the SH-2 CPU clock speed. Lower values improve performance but may cause slowdowns; higher values may reduce lag in CPU-heavy games. Values other than 100% may lower compatibility with some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_rtc_mode.Description
data.value: Virtual: clock advances with emulation (correct for fast-forward/save states). Host: syncs to real time.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_cartridge.Description
data.value: Select the cartridge to insert. 'Auto' uses the game database to pick the correct one. DRAM carts are required by many fighting games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_threaded_vdp1.Description
data.value: Run the VDP1 renderer in a dedicated thread for improved performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_threaded_vdp2.Description
data.value: Run the VDP2 renderer in a dedicated thread. Highly recommended for performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_deinterlace.Description
data.value: Render interlaced high-res modes in progressive mode. May cause artifacts in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_threaded_deinterlacer.Description
data.value: Run the deinterlacer in a dedicated thread. Requires threaded VDP2 and deinterlace enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_transparent_meshes.Description
data.value: Render mesh patterns as semi-transparent instead of checkerboard.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_audio_interpolation.Description
data.value: Linear interpolation matches real hardware. Nearest neighbor is harsher.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_threaded_scsp.Description
data.value: Run the SCSP and its MC68EC000 sound CPU in a dedicated thread for improved performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_audio_step_granularity.Description
data.value: Controls SCSP emulation accuracy. Higher values are more accurate but slower.

data.name: Emulation.Option.ymir.ymir_cdblock_lle.Description
data.value: Use low-level CD block emulation for improved accuracy. Requires CD block ROM in system directory.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bluemsx.bluemsx_msxtype.Description
data.value: Manually select the machine type you would like the core to start in.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bluemsx.bluemsx_vdp_synctype.Description
data.value: Match the game/machine region frequency to avoid emulated speed issues.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bluemsx.bluemsx_nospritelimits.Description
data.value: Remove the 4 sprite per line limit which can reduce or remove sprite flicker in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.bluemsx.hard_reset_f12
data.value: Use F12 to hard reset and restart emulation

data.name: Emulation.Option.bluemsx.hard_reset_f12.Description
data.value: Use key F12 to hard reset and restart emulation like blueMSX standalone

data.name: Emulation.Option.bluemsx.bluemsx_cartmapper.Description
data.value: When a ROM game or application is in the database, the emulator uses the databases to apply the correct mapper. If the sha1 value of a dump is not yet in the databases, it uses an automatic mapper detection system, but it can fail in some cases. In this situation, you can manually select the correct mapper.
